title: Microsoft Edge: Rewrite by Copilot (Writing Assistance) gains enterprise data protection
summary: The briefing correctly reports the planned rollout, default availability and documented controls, and distinguishes the policy names used by Message center and Learn. The WorkIQ sentence should retain Microsoft's qualification about content permissions and tenant controls.

claims.quote: Searched: "InlineComposeEnabled" Edge policy; "InlineComposeEnabled" "policy" "Edge". Read ComposeInlineEnabled reference and Edge policy-list search excerpts; they document ComposeInlineEnabled, not InlineComposeEnabled.

Path (Mandatory): SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge
Value name: ComposeInlineEnabled

Example registry value
0x00000000

claims.claim: Commercial Writing requires a Microsoft Entra account and is unavailable with personal Microsoft accounts.

claims.quote: Applies to a profile that is signed in with a Microsoft account: No

claims.claim: When ComposeInlineEnabled is unconfigured, writing features are available by default subject to feature availability and other applicable policies.
claims.quote: If you don't configure this policy, these Writing features are available by default, subject to feature availability and other applicable policies.

claims.claim: Enabling the policy permits eligible users to use the writing features, subject to availability and other policies.
claims.quote: If you enable this policy, eligible users can use these Writing features, subject to feature availability and other applicable policies.

claims.claim: When the policy is enabled, users cannot turn Commercial Writing off in Edge settings.
claims.quote: If you enable this policy, eligible users can use these Writing features, subject to feature availability and other applicable policies. Users can't turn Commercial Writing off in Microsoft Edge settings.

claims.claim: With the policy unconfigured, users can turn Commercial Writing off using Collaborate with Copilot as you write on the web in Edge settings.
claims.quote: Users can turn Commercial Writing off using 'Collaborate with Copilot as you write on the web' in Microsoft Edge settings.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance guidance; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The Edge management service exposes AI-generated text and editing on its Copilot tab.
claims.quote:
In the Microsoft Edge management service, select the Copilot tab
AI-generated text and editing: Provides AI-generated text creation and editing for eligible text fields.

claims.claim: No API or PowerShell surface for the Edge management service AI-generated text and editing setting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Edge management service "AI-generated text and editing" API Graph PowerShell; "AI-generated text and editing" "policy" API. Read Configuring Copilot Features and Graph Edge API overview excerpts; no automation for this setting.

claims.claim: Edge management service Copilot feature choices are assigned through a new or existing configuration policy.
claims.quote: select the Copilot tab, then use each dropdown to select Enabled or Disabled and assign the changes to either a new or existing configuration policy.

claims.claim: The cited Edge management service page does not name Rewrite, Writing Assistance, InlineComposeEnabled or ComposeInlineEnabled.
claims.quote: Searched: "AI-generated text and editing" "ComposeInlineEnabled". Read the complete Configuring Copilot Features page; it lists AI-generated text and editing without any of the four names or an explicit mapping to this change.

claims.claim: The Purview path is Data loss prevention > Settings > Data Loss Prevention > Endpoint DLP settings > Browser and domain restrictions to sensitive data > Sensitive service domain groups.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Data loss prevention > Settings (gear icon in the upper left hand corner) > Data Loss Prevention > Endpoint DLP settings > Browser and domain restrictions to sensitive data > Sensitive service domain groups.

claims.claim: No PowerShell or other automation equivalent for configuring sensitive service domain groups was found in Microsoft documentation.
claims.quote: Searched: "sensitive service domain groups" "PowerShell"; site:learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchangepowershell "sensitive service". Read the cited Purview procedure and endpoint-settings excerpts; no group configuration command.

claims.where: Risk assessment; controls[3].note; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: The cited Copilot page-content-access chart describes the Edge for Business sidepane experience.
claims.quote: This chart covers the behavior of Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat in Edge for Business which is accessible in the sidepane.

claims.claim: The sidepane page documents Purview and Intune MAM policy settings that block Copilot access to page content.
claims.quote: Edge for Business is integrated with Microsoft Purview and Intune MAM to provide Copilot blocking mechanisms through DLP. The table below outlines all the policies and their setting value for which Copilot will be BLOCKED from accessing page content.

claims.where: controls[3].note; Risk assessment; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not explicitly confirmed that the exact sidepane DLP settings list applies unchanged to Writing Assistance.
claims.quote: Searched: "Writing Assistance" "DLP" "Edge"; "Rewrite" "enterprise data protection" "Edge". Read MC1146821, ComposeInlineEnabled and Copilot page-content-access chart; the first two state DLP blocking generally, while the chart explicitly covers the sidepane.

claims.claim: The cited Learn pages do not describe the feature-specific implementation of enterprise data protection.
claims.quote: Searched: "Rewrite" "enterprise data protection" "Edge". Read the four cited Learn pages, Manage Copilot Chat and EDP search excerpts; they give controls or general protections, not an implementation explanation for Writing Assistance.
